Synopsis:
    Active US-Iran military hostilities have flared, with US strikes on Iran's Larak Island triggering Iranian retaliatory drone and missile attacks on US bases in the UAE and Jordan. Iran's IRGC is mining and threatening the Strait of Hormuz — a critical chokepoint for global energy flows handling roughly 20% of world oil and LNG transit. Iran's moderate president signals diplomatic openness while hardliners push confrontation and Hormuz tolling rights. The US is simultaneously escalating economic pressure via Operation Economic Outcast and the G20, threatening sanctions on any country trading with Iran — with China (Iran's primary oil buyer) in the crosshairs ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. Kharg Island (90% of Iran's crude exports) has been targeted rhetorically by Trump. The EU is aligned with US economic pressure strategy. Internal Iranian divisions, UAE drone intercepts, and stalled Lebanon/Gaza ceasefires compound regional instability.
